chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The prescribed penalty (hadd) of stoning is applied when four testify that they saw him insert and withdraw.

key_terms.حَدُّ الرَّجْمِ: Hadd of rajm — the prescribed Quranic/Sunnaic penalty of stoning for proven adultery (zina al-muhsan) committed by a married person
key_terms.يَشْهَدَ أَرْبَعَةٌ: Four must testify — the requirement of four adult male Muslim witnesses to establish this hadd punishment
key_terms.يُدْخِلُ وَ يُخْرِجُ: Insert and withdraw — the technical legal expression indicating direct witness of the act of penetration, the standard for establishing zina

ai.seo_question: How many witnesses are required for the hadd of stoning in Islamic law according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) lays down the evidentiary standard required to establish the hadd punishment of stoning (rajm) for adultery (zina). He specifies that four witnesses must testify that they directly observed the act of penetration and withdrawal. This ruling reflects the extremely high burden of proof in Islamic criminal law — requiring four eyewitnesses to actual intercourse — which effectively makes this punishment almost impossible to establish through testimony alone, reflecting the Sharia's emphasis on protecting privacy and deterrence rather than enforcement.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Penalty (Hadd) of the stoning is applied when four testify that they have seen him go in and come out’.
